q: LeetCode 判题系统的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core functional requirements should a LeetCode-style judging system support? (Select all that apply)
options: 支持浏览题目列表
支持在线编写并运行多语言代码
提交后能返回判题结果
展示竞赛的实时排行榜
why: 这四点覆盖题库浏览、编辑运行、判题反馈和竞赛展示，是 LeetCode 判题系统的主线功能。
why_en: The four core features are browsing problems, editing and running code, judging submissions, and showing contest leaderboards.
options_en: Let users browse a list of coding problems.
Let users write and run code in multiple languages.
Return a judged result after a submission.
Show a live leaderboard during contests.
optionExplanations: 用户得先能刷到题目列表才会点进去做题，这是最基础的入口功能。
编辑器要支持多语言编写和试跑，用户才能在提交前先验证思路。
提交之后必须给出通过或失败的判定，否则用户无法知道自己写对没写对。
竞赛模式需要排行榜才能体现名次和竞争，这是竞赛玩法的核心展示面。
optionExplanations_en: Users need to browse the problem list before they can pick something to solve, it is the entry point of the product.
The in-browser editor must support writing and running code in multiple languages so users can sanity-check logic before submitting.
A submission has to come back with a pass or fail verdict, or users have no way to know whether their solution actually works.
Contests need a leaderboard to show standings and competition, without it contest mode has no visible payoff.

scenario: 系统面向几十万用户、约 4000 道题目，竞赛峰值可达 10 万用户；需要安全运行不可信代码。
scenario_en: The system serves hundreds of thousands of users and about four thousand problems, contests can peak around one hundred thousand users, and it must safely run untrusted code.
q: LeetCode 判题系统的关键非功能需求有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which non-functional requirements matter most for a LeetCode-style judging system? (Select all that apply)
options: 运行用户代码时要隔离并保证安全
所有排行榜读都必须强一致到毫秒级
提交结果应在约 5 秒内返回或可查询
需要支撑约 10 万用户量级的竞赛
why: 重点是安全执行代码、5 秒级反馈和竞赛峰值；排行榜允许几秒级近实时，不需要毫秒级强一致。
why_en: The design centers on secure code execution, five-second feedback, and contest-scale traffic, while the leaderboard only needs near-real-time freshness, not millisecond consistency.
options_en: Isolate and secure the execution of user-submitted code.
Every leaderboard read must be strongly consistent within milliseconds.
Submission results should return or be queryable within about five seconds.
The system should support contests at roughly one hundred thousand users.
optionExplanations: 不可信代码必须先被隔离，否则一次提交就可能威胁到整个服务。
排行榜其实不需要毫秒级强一致，几秒的近实时刷新就够用，当成强一致需求会逼出不必要的重设计。
5 秒是判题给出的明确响应目标，直接决定了执行和查询链路要多快。
10 万用户是竞赛峰值的规模上限，决定了容量规划要按这个量级来做。
optionExplanations_en: Untrusted code has to run isolated first, or one bad submission could threaten the whole service.
The leaderboard does not actually need millisecond consistency, a few seconds of near-real-time freshness is enough, and treating it as a strong-consistency requirement forces needless redesign.
Five seconds is the stated response target, and it directly drives how fast the execution and query path has to be.
One hundred thousand users is the stated contest peak, and it sets the scale that capacity planning has to target.

q: 为什么说 LeetCode 判题系统相对多数系统设计真题规模偏小？
q_en: Why is a LeetCode-style judging system smaller than many system-design interview systems?
options: 用户和题目规模都远小于亿级平台
这套系统其实完全没有注册用户
所有提交的代码都完全不需要真正运行
竞赛排行榜自上线后就从未更新过
why: 规模判断会影响架构取舍：偏小系统不必一开始就做重度微服务拆分。
why_en: Recognizing the modest scale matters because a small system does not need heavy microservice decomposition from day one.
options_en: User count and problem count are both far smaller than a billion-item platform.
This system actually has no registered users at all.
Submitted code never actually needs to run.
The contest leaderboard has never updated since launch.
optionExplanations: 用户和题目量级都远低于动辄上亿的社交或电商平台，规模判断决定要不要一上来就上重架构。
系统其实有几十万注册用户，说完全没有用户直接和题设矛盾。
判题的核心恰恰是真实运行用户代码，说代码不需要运行等于否定了这道题存在的意义。
竞赛排行榜按比赛节奏定期刷新，说它从未更新过只是编造的反例。
optionExplanations_en: User and problem counts sit far below billion-scale social or e-commerce platforms, and that scale call decides whether you need heavy architecture on day one.
The system actually has hundreds of thousands of registered users, so claiming there are none contradicts the given setup outright.
Actually running submitted code is the whole point of judging, saying code never runs denies the reason this system exists.
The contest leaderboard refreshes on a regular cadence during the contest, so claiming it never updates is simply a fabricated claim.

q: LeetCode 判题系统最先要对齐的核心实体有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core entities should be aligned first for a LeetCode-style judging system? (Select all that apply)
options: Problem：题面、代码模板和测试用例
PaymentInvoice：购买记录
Submission：用户代码和运行结果
Leaderboard：竞赛排名
why: Problem 支撑浏览和编辑，Submission 支撑判题反馈，Leaderboard 支撑竞赛展示；支付记录不在这个产品范围内。
why_en: Problem, Submission, and Leaderboard map directly to browsing, judging, and contest display, while purchase records fall outside this product's scope.
options_en: Problem: statement, code stubs, and test cases.
PaymentInvoice: purchase records.
Submission: user code and its run result.
Leaderboard: contest rankings.
optionExplanations: Problem 承载题面、模板和测试用例，是浏览和编辑两条路径共同依赖的实体。
支付发票不在这个产品的功能范围内，把它列成核心实体是把电商模型硬套进判题系统。
判题结果必须挂在某条 Submission 记录上，它是连接用户、题目和结果的枢纽实体。
竞赛排名需要独立于 Problem/Submission 的实体来承载，否则没地方存名次和 tie-break 信息。
optionExplanations_en: Problem holds the statement, stub, and test cases, both browsing and editing depend on it.
Payment invoices are outside this product's scope, treating it as a core entity forces an e-commerce model onto a judging system.
Judging feedback has to attach to a Submission record, it is the hub entity tying together user, problem, and result.
Contest rankings need their own entity separate from Problem and Submission, or there is nowhere to store standings and tie-break data.

q: 补全 Problem schema 的关键字段：
q_en: Fill in the key fields in the Problem schema:
text: Problem 通常包含 {{id/title/question/level/tags}}、多语言 {{codeStubs}}，以及语言无关的 {{testCases}}。
why: 代码模板服务编辑器，测试用例服务判题；列表页只需返回这些字段的子集。
why_en: A problem stores metadata, language-specific code stubs, and language-neutral test cases for judging.

scenario: 用户打开题库首页，只需要题目摘要，不应一次返回完整题面和所有测试用例。
scenario_en: A user opens the problem-list page and only needs summaries; the API should not return full statements and all test cases at once.
q: 题目列表接口该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the problem-list API be designed?
options: GET /problems -> Problem[]（不分页，每次返回完整题面和全部测试用例）
GET /problems?page=1&limit=100 -> Partial<Problem>[]
GET /problems/:id（只能按 id 单条查询，做不了列表分页）
POST /problems（用写语义实现只读列表查询）
why: 列表页只需要标题、难度、标签等摘要字段，加分页避免一次渲染过多题目。
why_en: The problem-list endpoint should return paginated summaries with just title, difficulty, and tags rather than full content.
whenOtherWins: 如果是管理员批量导出题库，返回完整 Problem 的接口才有意义。
tradeoff: 摘要分页读取 vs 一次返回完整题面
options_en: GET /problems -> Problem[], with no pagination, returning the full statement and all test cases every time.
GET /problems?page=1&limit=100 -> Partial<Problem>[].
GET /problems/:id, which only fetches one problem and cannot paginate a list.
POST /problems, using write semantics for a read-only list query.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只包含某类型部分字段的 TypeScript 类型标注。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partial<T> is a TypeScript type that includes only some fields of type T.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把长列表拆成多页返回，避免一次传输过多数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pagination splits a long list into pages instead of returning everything at once.

optionExplanations: 如果是管理员批量导出全部题库，才值得每次都返回完整 Problem，否则列表页平时用不上这么重的响应。
摘要字段配分页正好卡住列表页的真实需求，不多传一个字段。
只能按 id 查单条的接口撑不起分页列表，翻页、排序这些列表页功能全做不了。
只读查询该走 GET 才能被缓存和安全重试，用 POST 表达列表读取是语义用反了。
optionExplanations_en: Returning the full Problem payload every time only pays off for an admin bulk export, the everyday list page does not need that much weight.
Summary fields plus pagination match exactly what the list page needs, without shipping a single extra field.
A single-item, id-only endpoint cannot support a paginated list, you lose paging and sorting entirely.
A read-only query should be a GET so it can be cached and safely retried, using POST here inverts the HTTP semantics.

scenario: 用户点击一道题并选择 Python 或 JavaScript，需要拿到完整题面和对应语言模板。
scenario_en: A user opens one problem and chooses Python or JavaScript, so the page needs the full statement plus the matching code stub.
q: 题目详情接口该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the problem-detail API be designed?
options: GET /problems/:id（不带 language，永远返回默认语言模板）
GET /problems?title={title}&language={language}（用标题当查找键）
GET /problems/:id?language={language}
POST /problems/:id/language（用 POST 切换语言状态）
why: language 参数让服务端按需返回代码模板，避免客户端硬编码所有语言的题面。
why_en: The language query parameter lets the server return the right code stub instead of the client hardcoding every language's version.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有模板都预先打包进客户端，也可以只返回题面本体，但服务端集中存模板更好维护。
tradeoff: 服务端按需渲染语言模板 vs 客户端预置全部模板
options_en: GET /problems/:id without a language parameter, always returning the default stub.
GET /problems?title={title}&language={language}, looking the problem up by title.
GET /problems/:id?language={language}.
POST /problems/:id/language, treating language selection as a stateful write.
optionExplanations: 用户已经明确选了语言，接口却忽略这个参数只给默认模板，等于丢掉用户的选择。
标题不是稳定唯一键，可能重名或改名，只有 id 才能可靠定位一道题。
用 id 定位题目、用 query 参数选语言，两件事各司其职，接口设计干净。
选语言只是读取偏好，不改变服务端状态，用 POST 把它当写操作是语义误用。
optionExplanations_en: The user explicitly picked a language, but ignoring the parameter and always returning the default stub throws that choice away.
A title is not a stable unique key, it can collide or change, only the id reliably locates one problem.
The id locates the problem and the query parameter picks the language, each does one job, which keeps the endpoint clean.
Picking a language is just a read preference that changes no server state, treating it as a POST write misuses the verb.

scenario: 用户提交某题代码，后端需要知道题目、语言和代码，但不能信任客户端传来的 userId。
scenario_en: A user submits code for one problem; the backend needs the problem, language, and code, but must not trust a client-supplied userId.
q: 提交接口该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the code-submission API be designed?
options: GET /submit?userId=123&code=...（把代码和身份放进查询参数）
POST /submit，body 里带 submittedAt 和 userId（时间戳和身份完全由客户端自行指定，未经服务端校验）
DELETE /problems/:id（提交等价于删除题目）
POST /problems/:id/submit，body 只带 code 和 language，userId 来自 session/JWT
why: 用户身份和时间戳属于服务端可信上下文，客户端只应提交代码和语言选择。
why_en: User identity and timestamps belong in trusted server context, so the client should only submit code and a language choice.
whenOtherWins: 只有无认证的内部管理工具才可能显式传 user id，面试默认用户已认证。
tradeoff: 身份和时间来自服务端会话 vs 由客户端自报
options_en: GET /submit?userId=123&code=..., putting code and identity in the query string.
POST /submit with submittedAt and userId entirely set by the client in the body, with no server-side check.
DELETE /problems/:id, treating a submission as a delete.
POST /problems/:id/submit with only code and language in the body; userId comes from the session or JWT.

termDefinitions.meaning: JSON Web Token（JWT）：一种在客户端和服务端间携带已认证身份信息的令牌格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JSON Web Token is a token format that carries authenticated identity information between client and server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端为已登录用户维护的可信状态，用来推导用户身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session is server-side trusted state used to derive the identity of a logged-in user.

optionExplanations: GET 不该带副作用，而且把身份塞进查询参数会被日志、代理和浏览器历史记录下来，泄露风险很大。
客户端可以随意伪造 userId 或 submittedAt，用它们判分等于把公平性交给了不可信的一方。
提交代码和删除题目是完全不同的语义，用 DELETE 表达提交会让接口读不懂。
身份和时间该来自服务端会话或 JWT 这类可信上下文，客户端只负责传代码和语言。
optionExplanations_en: GET should not carry side effects, and stuffing identity into query params gets logged by servers, proxies, and browser history, a real leak risk.
A client can forge userId or submittedAt at will, so trusting them for scoring hands fairness to an untrusted party.
Submitting code and deleting a problem are entirely different operations, using DELETE for a submit makes the endpoint's intent unreadable.
Identity and timing should come from a trusted server-side context like a session or JWT, the client only needs to send code and language.

q: 把 userId 或 submittedAt 作为客户端请求参数传入，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of accepting userId or submittedAt from the client?
options: 客户端可以篡改身份或时间，破坏安全性和排名公平性
数据库字段长度不够存这些值，需要额外扩容
判题容器会因此拒绝启动
排行榜会因此自动刷新更快
why: 客户端输入不可信；身份应来自认证上下文，时间应由服务器生成。
why_en: Client input cannot be trusted, so identity should come from authentication context and timestamps from the server.
options_en: A client can forge its identity or timestamp, breaking security and fair ranking.
The database columns are not wide enough to store these values, needing extra capacity.
The judging container would refuse to start because of this.
The leaderboard would automatically refresh faster because of this.
optionExplanations: 这正是不信任客户端参数的核心原因，身份和时间一旦能被伪造，安全和排名公平就同时崩了。
字段存不存得下是存储层的细节问题，跟谁提供这个值、能不能被信任完全是两回事。
判题容器要不要启动只看它有没有收到执行任务，跟请求参数来自哪里毫无关系。
轮询或刷新的频率是前端行为决定的，跟这两个参数来自客户端还是服务端没有因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly why client-supplied params cannot be trusted, once identity and time can be forged, both security and fair ranking collapse together.
Whether a column is wide enough is a storage detail, completely separate from whether the value can be trusted.
Whether a judging container starts depends only on whether it got a job, not on where the request parameters came from.
Refresh or polling frequency is a front-end behavior choice, unrelated to whether these two fields came from the client or the server.

scenario: 系统用户和题目规模不大，主要复杂点是安全判题，不想为小规模 CRUD 过早引入大量服务。
scenario_en: The user and problem counts are modest, the hard part is secure judging, and the first version should not split simple CRUD into many services too early.
q: 首版架构更适合什么？
q_en: What architecture fits the first version best?
options: 从第一天开始拆成几十个微服务
简单单体架构，加一个独立的代码执行组件
只用浏览器本地存储，不要后端
把判题和排行榜都交给第三方 SaaS，不自己实现
why: 两条约束一起看：安全判题是核心难点，不外包、放进隔离组件自己做；排行榜小规模就是 Redis sorted set，上 SaaS 是杀鸡用牛刀。所以单体保持简单，只隔离风险高的代码执行。
why_en: Two constraints together: secure judging is the core hard part, so do not outsource it, build it in an isolated component; a leaderboard at small scale is just a Redis sorted set, so a SaaS is overkill. So: a simple monolith with only the risky code execution carved out.
whenOtherWins: 如果团队规模、部署边界和流量都变大，再拆分 problem/submission/contest 等服务更合理。
tradeoff: 简单单体起步 vs 提前微服务化
options_en: Splitting into dozens of microservices from day one.
A simple monolith, plus one isolated code-execution component.
Browser-only local storage with no backend at all.
Outsourcing both judging and leaderboards to third-party SaaS instead of building them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大部分功能放进一个可独立部署单元的架构风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A monolith is an architecture style that keeps most functionality in one deployable unit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把系统拆成多个独立部署、各自负责一部分功能的服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Microservices split a system into multiple independently deployed services, each owning part of the functionality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把跑不可信代码的部分从主应用拆出来单独隔离——它是安全边界(不能和主应用同进程/同主机)、且负载不同(CPU 密集、突发)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The code executor is carved into its own isolated component because it is a security boundary (untrusted code must not share the main app process/host) and scales differently.

optionExplanations: 团队和流量规模都还撑不起几十个服务的运维负担，微服务在这个阶段只会增加协调成本。
复杂度只集中在代码执行这一个高风险组件，其余 CRUD 留在单体里反而更简单可维护。
判题和竞赛都需要服务端能被信任的状态，结果不能被用户随意改，纯本地存储做不到。
核心判题逻辑正是这道题要设计的差异化能力，外包给 SaaS 等于把这题最有价值的部分让出去。
optionExplanations_en: Team size and traffic do not justify dozens of services yet, microservices at this stage just adds coordination overhead.
Complexity concentrates in the one high-risk execution component, keeping the rest as simple CRUD in a monolith is easier to maintain.
Judging and contests both need trustworthy server-side state that a user cannot tamper with, pure local storage cannot provide that.
The judging logic itself is the differentiating capability this problem asks you to design, outsourcing it to a SaaS gives away the most valuable part.

scenario: 题目数量约几千，查询简单，测试用例可嵌入题目文档，暂时不需要复杂 join。
scenario_en: There are only a few thousand problems, queries are simple, test cases can live inside the problem document, and complex joins are not needed yet.
q: 题库应该选哪种存储？
q_en: What storage should the problem bank use?
options: 关系型数据库，用复杂 JOIN 管理题目和测试用例
图数据库，为题目之间建好友关系
DynamoDB 文档存储，嵌套测试用例
只用对象存储直接当查询数据库
why: 一道题是自包含的嵌套文档(描述+内嵌测试用例+各语言 stub)，按 id 取、一次读全、免 join——文档模型天生贴。不上 Cassandra：那是海量写/秒+查询优先的死板建模，几千道题读多写少用不上。关系库也行但要么拆表 join、要么塞 JSON。
why_en: A problem is a self-contained nested document (description + embedded test cases + per-language stubs) fetched by id in one read, no joins — a document model fits naturally. Not Cassandra: it is built for massive write throughput with rigid query-first modeling, overkill for a few thousand read-mostly problems. A relational DB works too but needs a join table or a JSON column.
whenOtherWins: 如果后续需要复杂 SQL 查询、事务或强关系建模，关系型数据库会更合适。
tradeoff: 嵌套文档简单读取 vs 关系型强查询能力
options_en: A relational database with complex joins to manage problems and test cases.
A graph database to model friendship relations between problems.
A DynamoDB document store nesting test cases inside each problem.
Plain object storage used directly as the query database.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 文档/键值数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL document and key-value database from AWS.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不依赖固定关系表结构、常按文档或键值组织数据的数据库类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL databases organize data as documents or key-value pairs instead of fixed relational tables.

termDefinitions.meaning: NoSQL：把一条记录存成 JSON 式嵌套文档，按 id 取、也能按字段查。代表：MongoDB(最经典)、DynamoDB、Couchbase、Firestore、Cosmos DB
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document store keeps each record as a nested JSON-like document, fetched by id or field. Examples: MongoDB (the classic), DynamoDB, Couchbase, Firestore, Cosmos DB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 宽列 NoSQL，为海量写入+水平扩展而生；建模按查询死板(query-first)、无 join；适合时序/事件流的巨量写，不适合几千道题的小型嵌套目录
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL for massive writes and horizontal scale, with rigid query-first modeling and no joins — great for huge write volumes, wrong for a small nested catalog.

rows: 事务 + join + 临时查询
自包含嵌套数据、按 id 取

optionExplanations: 这里没有复杂多表 JOIN 的查询需求，为几千条题目上关系型强一致反而是过度设计。
题目之间没有好友、关注这类社交图结构，图数据库的强项用不上。
访问模式就是按 id 或列表查询，测试用例天然可以嵌套存进同一份文档，NoSQL 文档模型正好贴合。
对象存储没有结构化查询和索引能力，直接当数据库用会让按 id 查询变得低效。
optionExplanations_en: There is no complex multi-table join need here, bringing in relational strong consistency for a few thousand problems is overkill.
Problems have no social-graph relationships like friendships or follows between them, so a graph database's strength goes unused.
The access pattern is just lookup by id or list, and test cases naturally nest inside one document, a NoSQL document store fits directly.
Object storage has no structured query or indexing, so using it directly as a database makes lookups by id inefficient.

why_en: Monaco Editor provides the in-browser coding experience but does not execute submitted code.
options_en: Redis Sentinel.
Kafka Connect.
CloudFront.
Monaco Editor.

q: 把用户提交的代码直接保存到 API Server 本地并执行，最大问题是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest problem with saving and running submitted code directly on the API server?
options: 安全、性能和隔离都不可接受，恶意代码可能破坏服务
执行会变慢但更安全
无法捕获程序的标准输出
数据库将无法写入 Submission 记录
why: 用户代码可能删数据、挖矿、发起网络请求、死循环或崩溃，不能和 API Server 同进程运行。
why_en: Untrusted code could delete data, mine cryptocurrency, make network calls, loop forever, or crash, so it cannot share a process with the API server.
options_en: Security, performance, and isolation all become unacceptable; malicious code can damage the service.
Execution becomes slower but safer.
It can no longer capture the program's standard output.
The database would be unable to write Submission records.
optionExplanations: 同进程执行不可信代码同时叠加安全、性能和隔离三重风险，恶意代码能直接碰到服务本身的进程和资源。
同进程执行只会更危险，不会因此变得更安全，这个说法把因果关系说反了。
能不能捕获 stdout 是执行环境本身的能力，跟它是否和 API Server 共享进程没关系。
写 Submission 表是判题流程的持久化步骤，跟代码在哪里执行是两件独立的事。
optionExplanations_en: Running untrusted code in the same process stacks security, performance, and isolation risk together, malicious code can touch the service's own process and resources directly.
Running in the same process only gets less safe, not more, this statement has the causality backwards.
Whether stdout can be captured is a property of the execution environment itself, unrelated to whether it shares a process with the API server.
Writing to the Submission table is the persistence step of judging, independent of where the code actually executes.

scenario: 需要比直接在 API Server 上执行更好的隔离，允许较高的启动成本。
scenario_en: The system needs better isolation than running code on the API server, and it can tolerate higher startup cost.
q: VM 方案的定位是什么？
q_en: What role does the VM approach play?
options: 隔离最弱，但启动最快
隔离强，但资源重、启动慢、生命周期管理成本高
完全无法重置或回收
只能运行 JavaScript 代码
why: VM 提供接近完整 OS 级的隔离，但每个 VM 带一份完整操作系统，启动和资源开销都比容器大。
why_en: A VM provides near-full OS-level isolation, but each VM carries a complete guest OS, making it heavier and slower to start than a container.
whenOtherWins: 如果安全隔离要求极高且能接受额外成本，VM 会比普通容器更稳妥。
tradeoff: 更强隔离边界 vs 更重的启动和资源成本
options_en: The weakest isolation but the fastest startup.
Strong isolation, but heavy resources, slow startup, and costly lifecycle management.
It can never be reset or reclaimed.
It can only run JavaScript code.

termDefinitions.meaning: Virtual Machine（VM）：带完整客户操作系统、运行在宿主机之上的隔离环境。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual machine is an isolated environment with a full guest operating system running on top of a host machine.

optionExplanations: VM 的隔离恰恰比容器更强而非最弱，说它隔离最弱是把两者的定位说反了。
带完整客户 OS 换来接近物理机级别的隔离边界，代价是启动慢、资源重，生命周期管理成本也更高。
VM 可以被快照、重置或回收复用，说它完全没法重置不符合虚拟化的基本能力。
VM 能装任意语言的运行时环境，语言限制不是 VM 方案本身的约束。
optionExplanations_en: A VM's isolation is actually stronger than a container's, not the weakest, this flips their actual positioning.
Carrying a full guest OS buys near-physical-machine isolation, at the cost of slow startup, heavier resources, and pricier lifecycle management.
A VM can be snapshotted, reset, or reclaimed for reuse, claiming it can never reset ignores basic virtualization capability.
A VM can host a runtime for any language, language restriction is not a constraint of the VM approach itself.

scenario: 要运行多语言用户代码，期望启动快、资源开销低，并能复用运行环境。
scenario_en: The system must run user code in many languages, with fast startup, low overhead, and reusable runtimes.
q: 多语言代码沙箱执行方案里，最终应该选哪种执行方式？
q_en: Which execution model should the multi-language code sandbox use?
options: 直接在 API Server 进程里执行
每次提交都启动一台完整虚拟桌面
按语言准备沙箱容器，由 worker 调用执行
只在用户浏览器本地运行，不上传服务端
why: 容器比 VM 轻量，能为 Python/JS/Java 等语言准备隔离运行时，配合资源限制控制风险。
why_en: Containers are lighter than VMs and can host isolated runtimes for Python, JS, and Java while resource limits keep risk in check.
whenOtherWins: 如果提交量极度突发且能接受冷启动，serverless function 也能托管这层执行环境。
tradeoff: 轻量容器复用 vs 更强隔离的完整虚拟机
options_en: Execute code directly inside the API server process.
Boot a full virtual desktop for every submission.
Prepare per-language sandbox containers that a worker invokes.
Run code only in the user's browser and never upload it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 共享宿主内核、只打包应用和依赖的轻量隔离环境。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A container is a lightweight isolated environment that shares the host kernel and packages only the app and its dependencies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 受控隔离环境：让代码在里面「随便玩」，但产生的影响都被边界圈在里面、漏不出去伤到外面。名字来自小孩玩的沙箱——沙子和捣乱都留在箱子里，不会弄脏客厅
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sandbox is a controlled isolated environment where code can do whatever, but its effects stay inside the boundary and cannot harm the outside — named after a child's play sandbox where the mess stays in the box.

termDefinitions.meaning: 沙箱=目标(给不可信代码一个受限隔离环境)；容器=实现手段之一(共享内核的轻量隔离)。容器要加固(seccomp/只读FS/限网)才算真沙箱；沙箱也可用 VM/microVM/WASM 实现
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sandbox is the goal (a restricted isolated environment for untrusted code); a container is one implementation. A container must be hardened to be a real sandbox, and a sandbox can also be a VM/microVM/WASM.

termDefinitions.meaning: 安全默认：每次提交起一个全新容器(编译+跑完它所有测试用例)，跑完销毁——不同用户的不可信代码不能共用一个活容器，防状态泄漏/串扰。为省冷启动可用 warm pool，但每次用完回收/重置成干净态
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Security default: each submission runs in a fresh container (compile + all its tests) then destroyed — untrusted code from different users must not share a live container. A warm pool cuts cold-start, but each slot is reset/recycled between submissions.

optionExplanations: 这正是要避免的同进程执行风险，判题和 API Server 共享进程会让恶意代码直接威胁服务本身。
完整虚拟桌面给的隔离和成本远超判题实际需要，量级不匹配。
按语言准备沙箱容器由 worker 调用，既比 VM 轻量、能复用，又比同进程方案多一层真实隔离。
客户端结果不可信，只在浏览器本地跑代码等于把判题公平性完全交给用户自己。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the in-process risk being avoided, sharing a process with judging lets malicious code threaten the service directly.
A full virtual desktop provides far more isolation and cost than judging actually needs, a scale mismatch.
Per-language sandbox containers invoked by a worker are lighter and reusable compared to VMs, while still adding real isolation over same-process execution.
Client-side results cannot be trusted, running code only in the browser hands judging fairness entirely to the user.

scenario: 提交负载难预测，希望云厂商自动扩缩每个语言运行时。
scenario_en: Submission load is unpredictable, and the team wants the cloud provider to autoscale each language runtime.
q: serverless 判题方案的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff of a serverless judging approach?
options: 完全没有任何进程或系统级隔离
必须一直运行一台昂贵的空闲机器
根本无法运行任何无状态函数
扩缩简单，但冷启动可能拖慢 5 秒反馈
why: Serverless 很适合弹性伸缩和托管运维，但冷启动和执行限制会威胁稳定的低延迟判题。
why_en: Serverless is great for elastic, managed scaling, but cold starts and execution limits can threaten stable low-latency judging.
whenOtherWins: 如果提交量稳定且要避免冷启动，常驻容器池更合适。
tradeoff: 免运维弹性伸缩 vs 冷启动带来的延迟风险
options_en: It provides no process- or system-level isolation at all.
It requires an expensive idle machine running at all times.
It cannot run stateless functions at all.
Scaling is simple, but cold starts can slow down the five-second target.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云厂商托管的函数/容器：你只管部署，平台按请求自动起实例、闲了缩到 0（scale to zero）——「扩缩简单」就是指你不用自建 worker 池/自动扩缩/容量规划
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A serverless function/container is provider-managed: you deploy, the platform auto-scales instances per request and scales to zero when idle — "simple scaling" means you build no worker pool, autoscaler, or capacity plan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有热实例可用时，平台要先起一个全新实例(拉镜像+启动运行时+初始化代码)才能处理请求，这段启动延迟就是冷启动(这里约 5 秒)；有热实例则是 warm start(快)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cold start is the startup delay (image pull + runtime init + code init, ~5s here) when no warm instance exists; a reused instance is a fast warm start.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先常驻 N 个热实例来消除冷启动——代价是要为这些空闲实例付费，等于放弃了 scale-to-zero 的省钱好处
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Provisioned concurrency keeps N instances warm to remove cold starts — at the cost of paying for idle instances, giving up the scale-to-zero savings.

optionExplanations: serverless 运行时依然有进程级隔离，说它完全没有隔离并不准确。
serverless 存在的意义正是省掉常驻空闲机器，这个说法和它的定位正好相反。
无状态函数正是 serverless 的本质设计，说它跑不了无状态函数是自相矛盾。
托管弹性伸缩省掉了运维负担，但代价是冷启动可能吃掉 5 秒反馈预算里的大半时间。
optionExplanations_en: Serverless runtimes still provide process-level isolation, claiming there is none is not accurate.
Serverless exists specifically to avoid an always-on idle machine, this statement contradicts its whole point.
Stateless functions are exactly what serverless is designed to run, saying it cannot is self-contradictory.
Managed elastic scaling removes ops burden, but the cost is a cold start that can eat up most of the five-second feedback budget.

q: 容器相对 VM 的核心性能优势是什么？
q_en: What is the core performance advantage of containers over VMs?
options: 共享宿主内核、不带完整 OS，因此更轻、启动更快
拥有比 VM 更完整的硬件虚拟化能力
完全不需要任何安全配置
只能运行一种编程语言
why: 容器共享宿主内核、只打包应用+依赖(不带完整 OS)，所以轻(MB)、启动毫秒级；VM 各带一份完整 OS、走 hypervisor 硬件虚拟化，重(GB)、启动秒级。代价：容器共享内核=隔离更弱，跑不可信代码要额外加固。
why_en: A container shares the host kernel and packs only the app + deps (no full OS), so it is light (MBs) and starts in milliseconds; a VM carries a full OS and virtualizes hardware via a hypervisor — heavy (GBs), starts in seconds. Trade-off: a shared kernel means weaker isolation, so untrusted code needs extra hardening.
tradeoff: 共享内核的轻量 vs 独立内核的强隔离
options_en: It shares the host kernel and skips a full guest OS, making it lighter and faster to start.
It provides more complete hardware virtualization capability than a VM.
It needs no security configuration at all.
It can only run one programming language.
optionExplanations: 共享宿主内核、跳过完整客户 OS，这正是容器比 VM 启动快、更轻量的根本原因。
完整硬件虚拟化恰恰是 VM 的强项，容器反而没有这层隔离。
共享内核反而需要额外加固，如 seccomp、只读文件系统，不是不需要安全配置。
换个语言镜像就能跑别的语言，容器本身对语言没有限制。
optionExplanations_en: Sharing the host kernel and skipping a full guest OS is exactly why containers start faster and stay lighter than VMs.
Full hardware virtualization is the VM's strength, not the container's, containers skip that layer entirely.
Sharing a kernel actually needs extra hardening like seccomp or a read-only filesystem, it is the opposite of needing no security config.
Swap in a different language's image and it runs a different language, containers themselves impose no language limit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 容器不带自己的 OS/内核，直接用宿主机内核，隔离靠 namespaces+cgroups——所以轻、快，但内核是共享的攻击面
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A container uses the host kernel (no own OS); isolation comes from namespaces+cgroups — light and fast, but the shared kernel is an attack surface.

termDefinitions.meaning: 虚拟机监控器：在硬件上虚拟出多台机器，每台 VM 跑自己完整 OS；隔离强但重、慢
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hypervisor virtualizes hardware into multiple machines, each VM running its own full OS — strong isolation but heavy and slow.

termDefinitions.meaning: Linux 内核隔离原语：namespaces 隔离视图(进程/网络/文件)，cgroups 限资源；容器隔离就靠它俩
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linux kernel primitives: namespaces isolate views (process/network/fs), cgroups cap resources — how containers isolate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 如 Firecracker/gVisor：VM 级隔离 + 接近容器的启动速度，判题/serverless 常用的「又安全又快」折中
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MicroVMs (Firecracker/gVisor) give VM-grade isolation with near-container startup — the safe-and-fast middle ground for judging/serverless.
